title: 34.3 A 4.75GHz Digital PLL with 45.8fs Integrated-Jitter and 257dB FoM Based on a Voltage-Biased Harmonic-Shaping DCO with Adaptive Common-Mode Resonance Tuning
problem: Digital PLLs for low-jitter synthesis must minimize DCO flicker and white noise, but voltage-biased DCOs require complex tuning-bank segmentation and extensive manual common-mode (CM) resonance tuning that is PVT-sensitive.
motivation: As SoCs integrate more high-speed converters and transceivers, each requiring dedicated low-noise synthesizers, PLL efficiency becomes critical; voltage-biased DCOs offer better noise-power tradeoffs than current-biased topologies but lack automatic CM control.
method: A voltage-biased DCO with harmonic-shaping architecture employs adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, enabling automatic foreground/background tuning across PVT variations. The approach uses wideband CM resonance expansion via transformer to maintain high CM impedance across the full tuning range.
key_novelty: Automatic adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, eliminating manual tuning complexity and improving PVT robustness.
contributions: Voltage-biased harmonic-shaping DCO with automatic CM-resonance tuning
Foreground/background adaptation for CM impedance across wide tuning range
Wideband CM resonance expansion ensuring high CM impedance during DCO frequency tuning
Achieves 45.8fs integrated jitter at 4.75GHz and 257dB FoM, enabling commercial-grade PLL designs
limitations: Integration with multi-band SoC and performance across corner conditions not fully discussed.
primary_theme: Voltage-biased DCO with automatic adaptive common-mode resonance tuning for low-jitter PLL
